subject: Request: carve-out for physical injury/property damage in Order Form
messages:
From: Diane Murray <diane.murray@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Carve-out for physical injury/property damage — Order Form

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's standard order form and came back with one substantive ask we need cleared before procurement can proceed: inclusion of an explicit carve-out from the limitation of liability for personal injury and physical property damage caused by vendor negligence or willful misconduct.

Our clause reads (summary): unlimited liability for bodily injury and physical damage to real property caused by vendor negligence, or a subcap tied to actual damages for physical harm. This is standard for our facility contracts since devices and integrations touch clinical systems.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is able to accept either (a) an unlimited liability carve-out for bodily injury/property damage, or (b) a limited carve-out with a subcap (please specify amounts) and proof of insurance?

Attaching our redlines for reference (Acme_MSA_Redlines.pdf). We need to close the PO this month.

Best,
Diane
Procurement — Acme Health Services
Attachments: Acme_MSA_Redlines.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -08:00

Hi Diane — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. I've looped in Marissa (legal) and Jordan (sales manager) to get us a proposed approach.

Quick context from my side: this is a hosted inference deployment integrated with Acme's clinical workflow for summarization. No on-prem hardware, but we recognize the risk profile. We want to be responsive while protecting the broader customer base and legal commitments.

Next steps: Legal will propose either (i) narrow carve-out language plus an insurance requirement, or (ii) a mutual insurance/indemnity structure. Jordan and I will review for commercial impact and precedent.

I'll follow up with a consolidated proposal by EOD Tuesday.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Carve-out for physical injury/property damage — Order Form

Soojin/Jordan — reviewed Acme's redlines. High-level: Acme's request for an unlimited carve-out for bodily injury/property damage is uncommon for SaaS contracts but understandable given clinical integration. We have a few defensible positions and a pragmatic compromise.

Options (recommended order):
1) Accept a narrowly tailored carve-out limited to "direct bodily injury or direct physical damage to real property" caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, subject to a subcap of $5,000,000 per occurrence / $10,000,000 aggregate. Require a certificate of insurance (commercial general liability or cyber-physical coverage) naming Acme as additional insured where available.

2) If Acme insists on unlimited exposure, require (a) explicit acceptance by revenue leadership (senior VP) and (b) a higher retained limit and/or escrow/indemnity holdback. We should avoid unlimited exposure without exec sign-off.

3) Alternative: keep overall liability cap (as in our MSA) but carve out bodily injury/property damage for third-party bodily injury claims only, and require Acme to prove proximate causation by our service. This is more protective but may be rejected by procurement.

Suggested redline (short form):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, neither Party's liability for direct damages arising from claims of bodily injury or physical damage to real property caused by such Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct shall be subject to the limitations set forth in Section [X], provided that Redwood's liability for such claims shall be limited to $5,000,000 per occurrence and $10,000,000 in the aggregate. Redwood shall, upon request, provide evidence of commercially reasonable insurance covering such exposures."

Commercial considerations: $5M subcap aligns with our current high-risk precedent but is higher than default SaaS caps. Jordan—this will reduce margin if accepted broadly; please confirm whether we can accept for Acme at that level as a one-off.

Attachments: OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (includes insertion in Section X, defined terms, and insurance proof language).

-Marissa
Corporate Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Carve-out for physical injury/property damage — Order Form

Agree with Marissa's approach. A couple of commercial notes:
- Precedent: we've accepted a $5M subcap for data-loss-adjacent physical risk in one previous healthcare deal (internal note: DEAL-HLTH-327).
- Upside: Acme is mid-sized but strategic; winning this will accelerate reference case.
- Mitigation: insist on COI (certificate of insurance) with minimum limits and name Acme as certificate holder. Also require prompt notice of claims and cooperation obligations.

If legal is comfortable, I'm fine offering the $5M/$10M subcap as a one-off, with an explicit "one-off" clause that prevents this being treated as new template language. Also propose a renewal clause tying the subcap review to contract renewals.

Jordan Blake
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Murray <diane.murray@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 13:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Carve-out for physical injury/property damage — Order Form

Hi Diane — thank you for your patience. After internal review we've got a compromise we believe addresses Acme's requirements while keeping commercial risk in check.

Proposed language (summary):
- Carve-out for bodily injury and physical damage to real property caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- Subcap: $5,000,000 per occurrence / $10,000,000 aggregate.
- Redwood to provide certificate of insurance evidencing commercially reasonable coverage (CGL or similar) within 10 business days of countersignature.
- This will be documented as a one-off concession for DEAL-ACM-4821 and will not constitute a change to our standard template absent exec approval.

Attached is the redlined Order Form (OrderForm_v3_redline.docx) with the inserted language. If this looks acceptable, I can send the DocuSign packet for signature (link below).

DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/12345abcdef

Let me know if you need the insurance carrier name/limits prior to countersignature — we can have our risk team prepare certified COI for your review.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: OrderForm_v3_redline.docx
